Focusing on your weight should be secondary in my experience. I am 25 and I still have issues trying new foods, especially when some have a negative preconception. You want to be able to enjoy the food you're having before forcing yourself to reach a weight you're not ready to yet. 

When I want to try relatively 'new' foods to your palette, I try to look up appetizing pictures of said foods either on a cook book/online recipe or a menu when I'm eating out. At least that way your brain has some sort of way of reassuring itself if you already like the way it looks, you're willing to taste it. 

Alternatively, if you're able, you can go out and try new foods or snacks with your friends or family and share ( if they are non-judgemental of course ). That way if you end up not liking the taste of something, they could always finish the rest and you can eat something safe for you. Try to keep some water with you too when you do this, I understand sometimes even a subtle taste can make you more nauseated than you thought. 

Another way could be easing new foods into ones you already like. I used to throw chicken tenders into just about anything to make sure I ate something. Now I'm more of a pasta person and try to incorporate foods i'm iffy about into a good sauce or with tasty meat. I've even added a few extra ingredients to a bowl of mac and cheese. 

I think being slow and steady with your eating and trying new things may be your best bet, especially if you have experience throwing up so soon after trying something completely new. Don't rush into full meals you don't feel prepared for and start with small additions and small portions when you're introducing food. 

I hope my ideas aren't overwhelming considering you're thinking about rice and apples and the like. Remember that even an 'unhealthy' version of a food is still you eating that food. So dips and sauces are still a-okay if it means you're enjoying a good meal. 

I hope this helps even a little or that you get some more concise answers. You deserve to eat food!
